subject: Checkout latency impact — request to confirm incident window and credit eligibility
messages:
From: Elena Rodriguez <elena@shopcart.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: payments@shopcart.com
Date: 2028-07-04T15:12:23-07:00
Subject: High checkout latency / intermittent failures 2028-07-04

Hi Priya,

We observed a sharp spike in checkout latency starting ~15:00 PDT today which caused ~6% of checkout requests to timeout in our production flows (several 504s and client-side timeouts). Our engineers captured traces that show backend inference calls to the recommendation endpoint took 8-12s during the spike (normal p95 ~300ms). This impacted order completion and payment authorizations.

Attached: a short CSV with timestamped error rates and a small log excerpt from our payment gateway showing patchy authorizations. Can you confirm whether Redwood had any known service degradation or deploy around that time and whether this would qualify for SLA credit? We need confirmation of the exact incident window and a preliminary severity classification for our procurement team.

Order of magnitude impact: ~1,200 affected checkout attempts between 14:58–15:22 PDT.

Thanks,
Elena
Senior Platform Engineer
ShopCart

(attachment: checkout_errors_20280704.csv)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena@shopcart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-04T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High checkout latency / intermittent failures 2028-07-04

Hi Elena — thanks for the timely heads-up and the CSV. I'm escalating this to our on-call infra team for immediate investigation.

I will confirm the incident window once we have server-side traces and an initial impact assessment. We will also check for any rolling deploys or autoscaling activity that could explain the spike.

Can you share the payment gateway traces you mentioned (if you can), and confirm whether the affected requests were routed to us in the US-west region? I'll treat this as a potential SLA claim and loop in our legal/procurement folks if needed.

I will follow up within the hour with an internal summary and next steps.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
(attachment: received-checkout_errors_20280704.csv)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-04T15:36:10-07:00
Subject: Fwd: High checkout latency / intermittent failures 2028-07-04 — please verify window + logs

Ben / Marissa — FYI from ShopCart (Elena). They report a ~24 minute spike starting ~14:58 PDT. They've sent a CSV with error rates, and noted increased p95 on our recommendation endpoint.

Immediate asks:
- Can infra confirm whether we had any in-flight deploys or autoscaler activity in us-west1 around 14:45–15:30 PDT?
- Pull invocation logs, prefix/KV cache warming traces, router fallbacks, and per-instance tail latencies. We need start/end timestamps that we can share with the customer.
- Quick classification request: outage vs degradation (per our SLO definitions) and preliminary severity (1/2/3).

Please include any evidence artifacts in the reply (log bundle, tail-sampled traces). This will be treated as a potential SLA credit request; I'll communicate findings to Elena and set expectations for a post-incident review.

Thanks — Priya

On 2028-07-04 15:12, Elena Rodriguez wrote: (see above)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-05T02:10:45-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High checkout latency / intermittent failures 2028-07-04 — preliminary findings

Summary (prelim): we've reproduced the spike. Preliminary root cause is an autoscaling/rolling-deploy interaction on a subset of recommendation-serving pods that caused a brief period of KV cache misses and request queueing. During scale-up we observed a backlog on the request queue for a small instance set which increased p95 dramatically until instances warmed and cache priming completed.

Estimated incident window (UTC and PDT):
- start: 2028-07-04T14:57:00-07:00 (2028-07-04T21:57:00Z)
- end: 2028-07-04T15:23:00-07:00 (2028-07-04T22:23:00Z)

Preliminary classification: Severity 2 (partial availability impacting a subset of requests / increased latency but not full region outage). Candidate for pro-rata credit under section 4.2 of the SLA depending on final verification of impacted request rates.

Attached evidentiary artifacts: redwood_logs_2028-07-04.tar.gz (trimmed invocation logs), latency_spike_window.csv (per-instance latencies), sample-tail-trace.txt (examples of long-latency traces).

Sample log excerpt:
[2028-07-04T21:58:12Z] instance-307 request_id=xyz latency=8123ms route=/recommendation cache_miss=true
[2028-07-04T21:59:01Z] instance-311 request_id=abc latency=9234ms route=/recommendation cache_miss=true

Next steps:
- I'll assemble a short post-incident timeline and remediation actions (patch to deploy coordination + cache prewarm).
- Product/infra to confirm whether any customer-specific routing or fallback caused amplification.
- Priya, if we confirm the window, we should offer ShopCart the SLA pro-rata calculation and an expedited postmortem (48–72h draft).

Ben
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood_logs_2028-07-04.tar.gz, latency_spike_window.csv, sample-tail-trace.txt)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena@shopcart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-05T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High checkout latency / intermittent failures 2028-07-04 — incident window & next steps

Hi Elena — thanks for the initial report and for sharing your data. Our infra team has completed a preliminary analysis (summary below).

What we found:
- Confirmed transient increase in p95 for the recommendation endpoint caused by autoscaler+deploy interaction.
- Incident window: 2028-07-04 14:57 PDT — 2028-07-04 15:23 PDT (26 minutes).
- Preliminary classification: Severity 2 (partial availability).

Eligibility for credit: based on the confirmed window and our SLA, the incident meets the threshold for a pro-rata uptime credit. We will calculate the credit using the standard SLA formula and apply it to your next invoice; the credit amount will be shared in writing and requires your approval.

Proposed next steps:
1) We will produce a 48–72 hour draft post-incident report covering timeline, root cause, and remediation plan.
2) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with infra and product to review the timeline and remediation steps.
3) We'll prepare the credit calculation and share a short reconciliation note.

Can you confirm you received the log bundle we attached? Also please confirm the billing contact to receive the credit reconciliation (I have payments@shopcart.com cc'd). Finally, would ShopCart prefer an expedited conference call tomorrow (2028-07-06) or a written report first?

Apologies for the impact — we are taking this seriously and will prioritize prevention fixes.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood_logs_2028-07-04.tar.gz, latency_spike_window.csv)

From: Elena Rodriguez <elena@shopcart.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: payments@shopcart.com
Date: 2028-07-05T10:01:12-07:00
Subject: Re: High checkout latency / intermittent failures 2028-07-04 — incident window & next steps

Thanks, Priya — that matches our timeline. We did receive the log bundle you attached and the sample traces were useful.

Please proceed with the 48–72 hour draft postmortem and the credit calculation. Payments@shopcart.com is the correct billing contact. We'd prefer the written report first; if there are any unresolved questions after that we can schedule a call.

Also please include an estimated date for when the credit will appear on our account and what the customer-facing statement will look like so our procurement team can track this internally.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Elena
Senior Platform Engineer, ShopCart
(attachment: none)
